docs.title: nf-meta
docs.text:
A reproducible representation, runner, and editor for metapipelines: Create chains of existing Nextflow pipelines and modules in an interactive browser-based editor and export into a YAML-based representation format. Validate and run the representation format with the integrated CLI tooling.

End-to-end Reproducibility

Community projects like nf-core curate a large number of reproducible best-practice pipelines, but projects frequently require running many pipelines back to back to produce insights. This typically involves ad-hoc scripting or manual intervention to start the next step, breaking the end-to-end reproducibility.

nf-meta represents the chain of analysis steps as a single .yaml file, declaring how one pipeline's outputs are consumed by the next to restore reproducibility.

Reduce complexity of pipelines

Pipelines should focus on their core analysis objective, instead of being concerned with what could possibly be run before or after. To facilitate multi-step analyses, there is pressure on individual pipelines to incorporate connection logic, potentially increasing their complexity and ultimately the maintenance burden.

nf-meta allows moving the connecting logic outside the scope of individual pipelines to reduce their complexity.

Runnable Provenance

Delegating data analysis work to agentic systems can take work off the shoulders of researchers. However, the interpretation of results requires knowing what exactly was run by the agent.

nf-meta can provide provenance of what was run that can be re-run if needed.

Harnessing by Validation

Agentic systems can handle the details of workflows like versions and param types better when given mechanisms to query for metadata and validate produced artifacts, rather than relying only on their internal state.

nf-meta offers metadata retrieval, caching of the important information, as well as upfront validation.

Automate the Repetitive

Some project types require frequently running the same set of workflows in sequence. While the transitions are well defined, this requires manual intervention at every step.

nf-meta offers a way to represent the full sequence of workflows with automated handoffs, and run it over the weekend.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
config_version: 0.3.0
workflows:
  n01:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: samples.csv
      outdir: out_fetchngs
  n02:
    from: n01
    name: nf-core/rnaseq
    version: 3.14.0
    params:
      input: ${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv
      outdir: out_rnaseq

nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml   # catch problems before running anything
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml        # execute the chain in dependency order
nf-meta editor metapipeline.yaml     # or edit it visually instead

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Validation before running. Static checks (does this reference a real workflow and param?) and, where reachable, checks against each pipeline's own nextflow_schema.json, before any compute is spent.
  • Cross-workflow references, so step N+1's params can point at step N's own resolved values instead of duplicating them.
  • A visual editor for building and updating configs as a graph, with full undo/redo, instead of hand-editing YAML.
  • Pluggable runners, so how the chain actually executes (wrap nextflow locally today, compile to one script or drive Seqera Platform tomorrow) is separate from the representation itself.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: This covers nf_meta.core (the config representation, validation, and graph), the runner plugin surface (nf_meta.runner), and the editor plugin surface (nf_meta.editor). Anything not listed here or in the config reference is internal: not part of the supported API, and may change without notice.

docs.title: Stability
docs.text:
nf-meta is beta: everything here can still change. Within that:

  • BaseRunner/RunOptions and BaseEditor/EditorOptions are the intended plugin extension points. See Writing a runner and Writing an editor plugin. These are the most deliberately designed part of the surface and change the least often, but are not yet under a formal compatibility guarantee.
  • nf_meta.core (the config model, validation, and graph) is documented so embedders can parse/construct/inspect metapipelines programmatically, but its shape still tracks the config format's own evolution (config_version) and is more likely to shift.
  • The built-in SimplePythonRunner and BrowserEditor are documented for reference, not as a base to subclass from. Extend BaseRunner/BaseEditor directly instead.

See the config reference for the .yaml format itself, which is the most stable part of the project: it has its own explicit version key (config_version) precisely so it can evolve without breaking existing configs.

docs.title: MetaworkflowGraph
docs.text:
MetaworkflowGraph()

The in-memory representation of a metapipeline: a directed graph of Workflow nodes plus shared GlobalOptions.

Mutating methods (add_workflow, add_transition, ...) validate the change immediately and raise GraphValidationError/ConfigValidationError rather than leaving the graph in an invalid state -- a failed mutation has no effect. Wrap a batch of mutations in deferred_validation() to validate once at the end instead of after each call.

Construct one via nf_meta.core.config.from_file/validated_graph rather than composing an empty graph by hand, unless you're building it up programmatically from scratch.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def __init__(self):
    self.G: nx.DiGraph = nx.DiGraph()
    self.global_options = GlobalOptions()
    self.config_version: str = CONFIG_VERSION_MAX
    self._events: list[Event] = []
    # None = not suspended. A set = suspended, accumulating the ids of
    # workflows touched while suspended, so deferred_validation's exit
    # can scope the batched dynamic check to only those (see validate()).
    self._validation_suspended: Optional[set[str]] = None

def pop_events(self):
    """Return and clear the events emitted by mutations since the last call.

    Used by `nf_meta.core.session.Session` to drive undo/redo history;
    most consumers don't need to call this directly.
    """
    events = tuple(self._events)
    self._events = []
    return events

docs.title: add_workflow
docs.text:
add_workflow(wf: Workflow)

Add a new workflow node.

Runs dynamic (network-backed) validation immediately unless inside deferred_validation(). Raises ConfigValidationError and leaves the graph unchanged if wf's id already has unresolved param references, or if dynamic validation reports an error.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def add_workflow(self, wf: Workflow):
    """Add a new workflow node.

    Runs dynamic (network-backed) validation immediately unless inside
    `deferred_validation()`. Raises `ConfigValidationError` and leaves the
    graph unchanged if `wf`'s id already has unresolved param references,
    or if dynamic validation reports an error.
    """
    if self._validation_suspended is not None:
        self._validation_suspended.add(wf.id)
    else:
        diagnostics = run_dynamic_checks(wf, previous=None)
        if any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in diagnostics):
            raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
        log_warnings(diagnostics)

    self.G.add_node(wf.id, workflow=wf.model_copy())

    try:
        if wf.params and self._validation_suspended is None:
            self.validate_param_references(wf)
        self._emit(WorkflowAdded(wf))
    except (GraphValidationError, ConfigValidationError) as e:
        self.G.remove_node(wf.id)
        raise e

docs.title: update_workflow
docs.text:
update_workflow(wf: Workflow)

Replace the workflow with wf.id with wf.

Same validation behavior as add_workflow. Raises ValueError if no workflow with that id exists yet -- use add_workflow to create one.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def update_workflow(self, wf: Workflow):
    """Replace the workflow with `wf.id` with `wf`.

    Same validation behavior as `add_workflow`. Raises `ValueError` if no
    workflow with that id exists yet -- use `add_workflow` to create one.
    """
    # TODO: Skip update if node unchanged? -> adds junk to history otherwise
    if wf.id not in self.G.nodes:
        raise ValueError("Workflow has invalid id. Update unsuccessful!")

    old_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(wf.id)

    if self._validation_suspended is not None:
        self._validation_suspended.add(wf.id)
    else:
        diagnostics = run_dynamic_checks(wf, previous=old_wf)
        if any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in diagnostics):
            raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
        log_warnings(diagnostics)
        if wf.params:
            self.validate_param_references(wf)

    self.G.nodes[wf.id]["workflow"] = wf.model_copy()
    self._emit(WorkflowUpdated(old_workflow=old_wf, new_workflow=wf))  # type: ignore

docs.text:
remove_workflow(wf_id: str, recursive=False)

Remove the workflow wf_id and every transition touching it.

Raises ValueError if wf_id doesn't exist. Does not remove workflows that only reference the removed one via ${wf_id:params:...} -- those become dangling references, caught on their own next validation.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def remove_workflow(self, wf_id: str, recursive=False):
    """Remove the workflow `wf_id` and every transition touching it.

    Raises `ValueError` if `wf_id` doesn't exist. Does not remove
    workflows that only reference the removed one via `${wf_id:params:...}`
    -- those become dangling references, caught on their own next
    validation.
    """
    if wf_id not in self.G.nodes:
        raise ValueError("Invalid wf_id")

    for edge in list(self.G.in_edges(wf_id)):
        self.remove_transition(*edge)

    for edge in list(self.G.out_edges(wf_id)):
        self.remove_transition(*edge)

    removed_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(wf_id)
    self.G.remove_node(wf_id)
    self._emit(WorkflowRemoved(removed_wf))  # type: ignore

docs.title: add_transition
docs.text:
add_transition(tr: Transition)

Add an edge marking tr.source as a predecessor of tr.target.

Raises GraphValidationError if either endpoint doesn't exist yet, or if adding the edge would introduce a cycle.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def add_transition(self, tr: Transition):
    """Add an edge marking `tr.source` as a predecessor of `tr.target`.

    Raises `GraphValidationError` if either endpoint doesn't exist yet,
    or if adding the edge would introduce a cycle.
    """
    self.validate_edge(tr.source, tr.target)

    if self.G.has_edge(tr.source, tr.target):
        print(f"[warning] Edge already exists: {tr.source}->{tr.target}")

    self.G.add_edge(tr.source, tr.target, transition=tr.model_copy())
    self._emit(TransitionAdded(tr))

    # can only be validated after-the-fact with the node in the graph
    if self._validation_suspended is None:
        self.validate_graph_topology()

docs.title: remove_transition
docs.text:
remove_transition(source: str, target: str)

Remove the edge source -> target, if present.

No-op (returns without raising) if the edge doesn't exist.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def remove_transition(self, source: str, target: str):
    """Remove the edge `source -> target`, if present.

    No-op (returns without raising) if the edge doesn't exist.
    """
    tr = self.get_transition(source, target)
    if not tr:
        return

    self.G.remove_edge(source, target)
    self._emit(TransitionRemoved(tr))

    if self._validation_suspended is None:
        source_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(source)
        self.validate_param_references(source_wf)  # type: ignore

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def update_global_options(self, glob: GlobalOptions):
    """Replace the graph's `GlobalOptions` wholesale. Not validated against
    individual workflows -- per-workflow effects (e.g. a shared `profile`)
    are only checked when that workflow is itself next validated."""
    old_globals = self.global_options
    self.global_options = glob
    self._emit(GlobalOptionsUpdated(new_globals=glob, old_globals=old_globals))

docs.title: validate_param_references
docs.text:
validate_param_references(wf: Workflow)

Check that every ${wf_id:params:key} reference in wf.params points at a real, already-resolvable predecessor param.

Raises ConfigValidationError (carrying one Diagnostic per bad reference) if any reference targets an unknown workflow, a workflow that isn't actually a predecessor of wf, or a param with no value.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def validate_param_references(self, wf: Workflow):
    """Check that every `${wf_id:params:key}` reference in `wf.params`
    points at a real, already-resolvable predecessor param.

    Raises `ConfigValidationError` (carrying one `Diagnostic` per bad
    reference) if any reference targets an unknown workflow, a workflow
    that isn't actually a predecessor of `wf`, or a param with no value.
    """

    def diagnostic(ref, message: str) -> Diagnostic:
        field = (
            f"params.{ref.source_key}"
            if isinstance(ref, WorkflowReference)
            else "params"
        )
        return Diagnostic(
            workflow_id=ref.source_wf_id,
            field=field,
            yaml_path=f"workflows.{ref.source_wf_id}.{field}",
            message=message,
            severity=Severity.ERROR,
        )

    diagnostics: list[Diagnostic] = []
    for ref in wf.field_refs:
        if ref.namespace != "params":
            continue  # output references not yet validated
        referenced_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(ref.target_wf_id)
        if not referenced_wf:
            diagnostics.append(
                diagnostic(ref, f"Reference to unknown workflow: {ref.target_wf_id}")
            )
            continue

        if ref.target_wf_id not in list(self.G.predecessors(wf.id)):
            diagnostics.append(
                diagnostic(
                    ref,
                    f"Reference to workflow {ref.target_wf_id} that is not a predecessor of {wf.id}",
                )
            )
            continue

        if not referenced_wf.params or not ref.target_key:
            diagnostics.append(
                diagnostic(ref, f"No referencable params in workflow {referenced_wf.id}")
            )
            continue

        if not referenced_wf.params.get(ref.target_key):
            diagnostics.append(
                diagnostic(ref, f"Reference to unresolvable param: {ref.target_key}")
            )

    if diagnostics:
        raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)

def validate_graph_topology(self):
    """Raise `GraphValidationError` if the graph contains a cycle."""
    # Detect cycles
    if not nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(self.G):
        cycle = nx.find_cycle(self.G)
        raise GraphValidationError(f"Workflow graph contains a cycle: {cycle}")

def validate_edge(self, src, tgt):

        raise GraphValidationError(f"Edge refers to nonexistent node: {src}->{tgt}")

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
validate(touched: Optional[set[str]] = None)

Fully re-validate the graph: topology, edge endpoints, workflow ids, and every workflow's param references.

Pass touched (a set of workflow ids) to also run a single batched dynamic (network-backed) validation pass scoped to just those workflows -- this is what deferred_validation() uses on exit, rather than dynamic-validating the whole graph on every batch. Raises GraphValidationError/ConfigValidationError on the first failure found; does not collect all errors across the whole graph in one call.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def validate(self, touched: Optional[set[str]] = None):
    """Fully re-validate the graph: topology, edge endpoints, workflow
    ids, and every workflow's param references.

    Pass `touched` (a set of workflow ids) to also run a single batched
    dynamic (network-backed) validation pass scoped to just those
    workflows -- this is what `deferred_validation()` uses on exit, rather
    than dynamic-validating the whole graph on every batch. Raises
    `GraphValidationError`/`ConfigValidationError` on the first failure
    found; does not collect all errors across the whole graph in one
    call.
    """
    self.validate_graph_topology()

    # Detect missing workflow nodes
    for src, tgt in self.G.edges():
        self.validate_edge(src, tgt)

    # Ensure workflow IDs are valid (non-empty)
    for n in self.G.nodes:
        if not isinstance(n, str) or not n:
            raise GraphValidationError("Workflow id must be a non-empty string.")

    for n in self.G.nodes:
        wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(n)
        self.validate_param_references(wf)  # type: ignore

    if touched:
        # Batched, concurrent dynamic check scoped to only the workflows
        # touched while suspended — not the whole graph. A node removed
        # later in the same suspended block is filtered out (nothing to
        # check).
        raw = [self.get_workflow_by_id(n) for n in touched if n in self.G.nodes]
        workflows = [wf for wf in raw if wf is not None]
        diagnostics = check_all(workflows)
        if any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in diagnostics):
            raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
        log_warnings(diagnostics)

def get_workflow_by_id(self, id: str) -> Optional[Workflow]:
    """Return the workflow with this id, or `None` if it doesn't exist."""
    try:
        return self.G.nodes[id].get("workflow")
    except KeyError:
        return None

def get_workflows_sorted(self) -> list[Workflow]:
    """Returns workflows in valid execution order."""

    workflows = [self.get_workflow_by_id(n) for n in nodes_sorted]

Filter workflows (default: get_workflows_sorted()) down to the sub-DAG reachable from start and able to reach target (inclusive on both ends). Omit either bound to leave that side unrestricted.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def subset_workflows(
    self,
    start: Optional[str] = None,
    target: Optional[str] = None,
    workflows: Optional[list[Workflow]] = None,
):
    """Filter `workflows` (default: `get_workflows_sorted()`) down to the
    sub-DAG reachable from `start` and able to reach `target` (inclusive
    on both ends). Omit either bound to leave that side unrestricted."""

    if workflows is None:
        workflows = self.get_workflows_sorted()

    if not len(workflows):
        return []

    if start:
        fw_reachable = nx.descendants(self.G, start) | {start}
        workflows = [wf for wf in workflows if wf.id in fw_reachable]

    if target:
        bw_reachable = nx.ancestors(self.G, target) | {target}
        workflows = [wf for wf in workflows if wf.id in bw_reachable]

    return workflows

def get_start_workflow(self) -> Optional[Workflow]:
    """
    Return the first order in topological sorting or None if no nodes exist
    """
    workflows_sorted = self.get_workflows_sorted()
    if not len(workflows_sorted):
        return None
    else:
        return workflows_sorted[0]

docs.title: deferred_validation
docs.text:
deferred_validation()

Suspend per-operation validation; on exit, run a full graph validation plus a single batched, concurrent dynamic-check pass scoped to the workflows touched while suspended (not the whole graph).

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
@contextmanager
def deferred_validation(self):
    """
    Suspend per-operation validation; on exit, run a full graph
    validation plus a single batched, concurrent dynamic-check pass
    scoped to the workflows touched while suspended (not the whole
    graph).
    """
    self._validation_suspended = set()
    try:
        yield self
    finally:
        touched = self._validation_suspended
        self._validation_suspended = None
        self.validate(touched)

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/config.py 
def from_file(cfg_file: Path, *, collect_errors: bool = False) -> "MetaworkflowGraph":
    """Read `cfg_file` as YAML and build+validate a `MetaworkflowGraph` from
    it. Reads the whole file into memory; makes no other side effects. See
    `validated_graph` for the validation contract and `collect_errors`."""
    with open(cfg_file) as fh:
        data = yaml.safe_load(fh)
    return validated_graph(data, collect_errors=collect_errors)

    """Write `g` to `file` as YAML (via `dump_config`), prefixed with a
    `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...` comment pointing at the published
    JSON Schema for editor autocompletion. Overwrites `file` if it exists."""
    with open(file, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(f"# yaml-language-server: $schema={SCHEMA_URL}\n")

docs.text:
dump_config(g: MetaworkflowGraph) -> dict

Project a MetaworkflowGraph back to the config's dict shape (the inverse of validated_graph): config_version, globals (omitted if empty), and workflows keyed by id with each workflow's own from: list reconstructed from the graph's edges. Always writes the current dict-keyed workflows: + per-workflow from: form, never the legacy list/top-level-transitions: shapes, even if the graph was loaded from one of those.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/config.py 
def dump_config(g: "MetaworkflowGraph") -> dict:
    """Project a `MetaworkflowGraph` back to the config's dict shape (the
    inverse of `validated_graph`): `config_version`, `globals` (omitted if
    empty), and `workflows` keyed by id with each workflow's own `from:` list
    reconstructed from the graph's edges. Always writes the current
    dict-keyed `workflows:` + per-workflow `from:` form, never the legacy
    list/top-level-`transitions:` shapes, even if the graph was loaded from
    one of those."""
    from_by_target: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for tr in g.get_transitions():
        from_by_target.setdefault(tr.target, []).append(tr.source)

    workflows_dict = {}
    for w in g.get_workflows():
        wf_dict = {k: v for k, v in w.model_dump_config().items()}
        if w.id in from_by_target:
            wf_dict["from"] = from_by_target[w.id]
        workflows_dict[w.id] = wf_dict

    config_dict = {
        "config_version": g.config_version,
        "globals": g.global_options.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
        if g.global_options
        else None,
        "workflows": workflows_dict,
    }

    if not config_dict["globals"]:
        del config_dict["globals"]

    return config_dict

docs.title: validated_graph
docs.text:
validated_graph(data: dict, *, collect_errors: bool = False) -> MetaworkflowGraph

Construct a MetaworkflowGraph from a raw, parsed-YAML config dict.

Workflows can be declared as a dict keyed by id (workflows: {<id>: {...}}, the preferred form) or as a legacy list of definitions each carrying their own id. Transitions are declared per-workflow via from: <id> or from: [<id>, ...]; a top-level transitions: key is also still accepted, but mixing both styles in the same file raises rather than merging them.

Both the list-format workflows: and the top-level transitions: key are deprecated -- reading either logs a CLI warning. Fix by opening and saving the config in the editor, which always writes the current dict-keyed workflows: + per-workflow from: form.

By default (collect_errors=False) this fails fast, raising on the first problem found. Pass collect_errors=True for a best-effort pass that collects every problem instead of stopping at the first -- used by the CLI's validate command.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/config.py 
def validated_graph(data: dict, *, collect_errors: bool = False) -> "MetaworkflowGraph":
    """Construct a MetaworkflowGraph from a raw, parsed-YAML config dict.

    Workflows can be declared as a dict keyed by id (`workflows: {<id>: {...}}`,
    the preferred form) or as a legacy list of definitions each carrying their
    own `id`. Transitions are declared per-workflow via `from: <id>` or
    `from: [<id>, ...]`; a top-level `transitions:` key is also still accepted,
    but mixing both styles in the same file raises rather than merging them.

    Both the list-format `workflows:` and the top-level `transitions:` key are
    deprecated -- reading either logs a CLI warning. Fix by opening and saving
    the config in the editor, which always writes the current dict-keyed
    `workflows:` + per-workflow `from:` form.

    By default (`collect_errors=False`) this fails fast, raising on the first
    problem found. Pass `collect_errors=True` for a best-effort pass that
    collects every problem instead of stopping at the first -- used by the
    CLI's `validate` command.
    """
    if collect_errors:
        return _full_validated_graph(data)
    return _fast_validated_graph(data)

docs.text:
validated_workflow(data: dict) -> Workflow

Construct and fully validate a single workflow from a flat, raw dict (id optional -- the model's own default_factory generates one if omitted). Runs the same tier-0/1 construction plus tier-2 dynamic checks a workflow gets as part of a full config build. Returns the validated Workflow, or raises GraphValidationError/ConfigValidationError.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/config.py 
def validated_workflow(data: dict) -> Workflow:
    """Construct and fully validate a single workflow from a flat, raw dict
    (`id` optional -- the model's own `default_factory` generates one if
    omitted). Runs the same tier-0/1 construction plus tier-2 dynamic checks
    a workflow gets as part of a full config build. Returns the validated
    Workflow, or raises `GraphValidationError`/`ConfigValidationError`.
    """
    if not data:
        raise GraphValidationError("No config data provided")
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise GraphValidationError(
            f"Expected a flat mapping, got {type(data).__name__!r}"
        )
    wf, diagnostics = construct_workflow(data, data.get("id", "<unknown>"))
    if wf is None:
        raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
    dynamic_diagnostics = run_dynamic_checks(wf, previous=None)
    errors = [d for d in dynamic_diagnostics if d.severity == Severity.ERROR]
    if errors:
        raise ConfigValidationError(errors)
    log_warnings(dynamic_diagnostics)
    return wf

Construct and validate a GlobalOptions block from a flat, raw dict. Returns the validated GlobalOptions, or raises GraphValidationError/ConfigValidationError.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/config.py 
def validated_globals(data: dict) -> GlobalOptions:
    """Construct and validate a `GlobalOptions` block from a flat, raw dict.
    Returns the validated `GlobalOptions`, or raises
    `GraphValidationError`/`ConfigValidationError`.
    """
    if not data:
        raise GraphValidationError("No config data provided")
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise GraphValidationError(
            f"Expected a flat mapping, got {type(data).__name__!r}"
        )
    try:
        return GlobalOptions(**data)
    except ValidationError as e:
        raise ConfigValidationError(
            diagnostics_from_pydantic_error(e, workflow_id=None)
        ) from e

One validation problem with a single field of a single workflow (or of globals, when workflow_id is None). The common vocabulary every validation tier (pydantic construction, dynamic/network checks, cross-workflow reference checks) reports through, so callers handle one shape regardless of where a problem originated.

ConfigValidationError(errors: list[Diagnostic], graph_messages: list[str] = list())

A workflow/config-definition-level validation failure, whether from tier-0/1 (pydantic construction), tier-2 (network-backed) checks, or cross-workflow reference validation. Every consumer treats all of these identically, so they share one exception type.

A structural problem with the graph itself: a cycle, an edge to a nonexistent node, or a malformed workflows:/from:/transitions: shape. Distinct from ConfigValidationError, which carries per-field Diagnostics about individual workflow/globals content.

docs.title: BaseEditor
docs.text:
BaseEditor(options: EditorOptions)

Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for all metapipeline editor backends.

Subclasses register themselves by defining an EDITOR_NAME class attribute. Registration happens automatically at class-definition time via __init_subclass__, so a new editor becomes available as soon as its module is imported, with no changes to the dispatch logic needed.

Example::

class MyEditor(BaseEditor):
    EDITOR_NAME = "my-editor"

    def start(self): ...

Subclasses should not override __init__. All EditorOptions fields are available via self.options.

        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} must define EDITOR_NAME = '...' as a class attribute"
        )
    self.options = options

docs.title: BaseRunner
docs.text:
BaseRunner(run_options: RunOptions)

Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for all metapipeline runner backends.

Subclasses register themselves by defining a RUNNER_NAME class attribute. The value is the string name used to select the runner::

class MyRunner(BaseRunner):
    RUNNER_NAME = "my-runner"

    def run(self, g): ...
    def resume(self, g): ...

Registration happens automatically at class-definition time via __init_subclass__. run_metapipeline looks up the concrete class from _REGISTRY, so a new runner becomes available as soon as its module is imported, with no changes to run_metapipeline needed.

Subclasses should not override __init__. The RunOptions passed in is stored as self.run_options, available to every runner without repeating the constructor.

def __init__(self, run_options: RunOptions) -> None:
    if "RUNNER_NAME" not in type(self).__dict__:
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} must define RUNNER_NAME = '...' as a class attribute"
        )
    self.run_options = run_options

docs.title: RunOptions dataclass
docs.text:
RunOptions(runner_name: str = 'python', cachedir: Path = Path('.nf-meta-cache'), verbose: bool = False, output_lines: int = 20, start: Optional[str] = None, target: Optional[str] = None, nf_profile: Optional[str] = None, stub: bool = False, resume: bool = False)

Runtime options that control how a metapipeline run is executed.

Constructed from CLI arguments and passed to the runner. All fields have sensible defaults so the dataclass can be instantiated without arguments for programmatic use.

Attributes:

Name Type Description runner_name str

Name of the runner backend to use. Must match a key registered in base_runner._REGISTRY.

cachedir Path

Directory used for all per-workflow working directories, resolved-param cache files, and Nextflow work directories. Created automatically if it does not exist.

verbose bool

Enables verbose logging output.

output_lines int

Number of most-recent output lines shown in the live scrolling panel while a workflow step is running. Only has an effect in the Python runner.

start Optional[str]

Workflow ID at which execution begins. Workflows topologically upstream of this node are skipped. Cross-boundary parameter references must be satisfiable from previously cached runs. None means start from all source nodes.

target Optional[str]

Workflow ID at which execution ends. Workflows topologically downstream of this node are skipped. None means run until all sink nodes.

nf_profile Optional[str]

Nextflow profile name (or comma-separated list of names) appended globally to every workflow invocation, taking precedence over per-workflow profile settings. Whitespace is stripped before passing to Nextflow.

stub bool

When True, passes -stub to every Nextflow invocation so that only the stub block of each process is executed. Useful for validating pipeline structure without real computation.

resume bool

When True, skips any workflow step whose working directory already contains a successful result (OUT.txt present, ERROR.txt absent) and passes -resume to Nextflow for workflow-level checkpoint resumption.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: The nf-meta package ships a browser-based editor for interactively visualizing and editing metapipeline configs. Autocompleted and validated forms for updating workflow attributes can make creating or extending workflow chains easier, if you are not used to hand-writing YAML directly. Because mistakes can happen, the edit history allows going back to a previous state or reapplying a change you made.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# start fresh
nf-meta editor 

# or open some existing work
nf-meta editor [path/to/metapipeline.yaml]

Note

The editor starts and continues to run a session which essential for the browser page to work. It will not terminate and block the current prompt until you do so manually. (Ctrl + C or Cmd + C)

This serves the editor's frontend and automaatically opens it in a browser tab, backed by a local session and state. (nf_meta.core.session) The session tracks graph mutations by updating the internal history, fetches data while keeping a local cache, and responds to validation requests. Passing no path starts a new, empty metapipeline.

docs.title: Editor backends
docs.text: The editor is extensible via plugins in the same way runners are: --editor <name> selects a registered BaseEditor subclass. The one described above is the only one shipped with nf-meta right now and opens by default. See Writing an editor plugin to add another.

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
The package is published to the Python Package Index and can be installed with your favorite dependency tool:

# with pip
pip install nf-meta

# with uv
uv add nf-meta

Note

nf-meta orchestrates Nextflow runs. It does not bundle Nextflow itself. Running a metapipeline (nf-meta run) requires a working nextflow on PATH, matching whatever globals.nextflow_version your config declares (if set). Validating a config (nf-meta validate) does not require Nextflow to be installed.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install with the dev dependency group:

git clone https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-meta
cd nf-meta
uv sync --group dev

docs.title: Editor frontend
docs.text:
The browser editor's frontend lives under src/nf_meta/editor/frontend and runs as a separate node server during development:

cd src/nf_meta/editor/frontend
npm install
npm run dev

With the frontend dev server running, launch the CLI in dev mode so it proxies to it instead of the bundled build:

NF_META_DEVMODE=1 uv run nf-meta editor [</path/to/metapipeline.yml>]

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text: uv run pytest

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This small guide will walk you through the smallest possible metapipeline that actually runs: a single workflow step, that executes the fetchngs pipeline to fetch some data from a public repository. The resulting metapipeline is validated and executed via the CLI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• nf-meta installed (see Installation)
  • Nextflow installed, required for nf-meta run but not for the nf-meta validate or editor commands.

docs.title: 1. Write a config
docs.text:
Create metapipeline.yaml:

config_version: 0.3.0
workflows:
  fetch:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/test-datasets/2732b911c57e607fa7aea5ba0c3d91b25bafb662/testdata/v1.12.0/sra_ids_test.csv
      outdir: results
  • config_version pins the representation's schema version. See Config reference.
  • fetch is the workflow's id, which can be referenced by another workflow step (see Cross-workflow references) and while running by --start/--target on the CLI.
  • name/version uniquely describe an nf-core pipeline. For a non-nf-core pipeline, the url field is required as well.

docs.title: 2. Validate it
docs.text:
nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml

During validation, first the config shape is checked statically for required keys, references, and graph layout. The config's static shape is also available as a JSON Schema your editor can check as you type. (See Editor autocompletion) Next, nf-meta tries to incorporate metadata provided by nf-core as well as in each pipeline's nextflow_schema.json file to validate urls, versions, and required parameters or types. You will get summarized validation feedback with line numbers and keys in your console.

docs.title: 3. Run it
docs.text:
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --stub

To just see that everything runs as expected, we use Nextflow's stub-run mechanism which replaces each process script with a no-op stub that requires no containers or environment. This Nextflow run options is resurfaced to the nf-meta run cli interface as the --stub flag. This can be useful to confirm the structure and parameter wiring resolves correctly without waiting on real compute or container pulls.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• A metapipeline with more than one steps, chained via references: see YAML representation overview.
  • Editing configs visually instead of by hand: see Editor.
  • nf-meta run --resume and per-workflow caching: see Python runner.

docs.title: Writing a runner
docs.text: A runner turns a validated MetaworkflowGraph into actual Nextflow execution. This walks through the minimum needed to add one as an installable plugin. See BaseRunner for the full contract.

docs.title: 1. Subclass BaseRunner
docs.text:
# my_runner_package/runner.py
from nf_meta.core.graph import MetaworkflowGraph
from nf_meta.runner import BaseRunner


class MyRunner(BaseRunner):
    RUNNER_NAME = "my-runner"

    def run(self, g: MetaworkflowGraph) -> None:
        for wf in g.get_workflows_sorted():
            ...  # execute wf, in dependency order

    def resume(self, g: MetaworkflowGraph) -> None:
        ...  # continue a previously interrupted run
  • RUNNER_NAME is required. Defining it is what registers the class (via BaseRunner.__init_subclass__), and it's the string users pass to --runner.
  • Don't override __init__. self.run_options (a RunOptions) is already set by BaseRunner.__init__; read self.run_options.cachedir, .stub, .start/.target, etc. from there.
  • Let failures raise. run_metapipeline doesn't catch exceptions from run/resume, so a workflow failure should propagate rather than being swallowed into a silent partial result.

docs.title: 2. Advertise it as a plugin
docs.text:
Registration only happens when the module defining MyRunner is actually imported. nf-meta discovers runner plugins via the nf_meta.runners entry-point group. Add this to your package's pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."nf_meta.runners"]
my-runner = "my_runner_package.runner:MyRunner"

Once installed alongside nf-meta, my-runner appears in nf-meta run --runner without any change to nf-meta itself.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
pip install -e .   # or however your plugin package installs
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --runner my-runner

If it doesn't show up, check that the entry point's module actually imports without error. _load_runner_plugins logs a warning (not a hard failure) and skips a plugin that fails to load, which can silently hide a broken import.

docs.title: Writing an editor plugin
docs.text: An editor backend is what nf-meta editor --editor <name> launches. This walks through adding one as an installable plugin. See BaseEditor for the full contract.

docs.title: 1. Subclass BaseEditor
docs.text:
# my_editor_package/editor.py
from nf_meta.editor import BaseEditor


class MyEditor(BaseEditor):
    EDITOR_NAME = "my-editor"

    def start(self) -> None:
        ...  # block until the user is done editing
  • EDITOR_NAME is required. Defining it registers the class (via BaseEditor.__init_subclass__) and is the string users pass to --editor.
  • Don't override __init__. self.options (an EditorOptions) is already set; read self.options.host/.port from there if your backend serves over HTTP.
  • start() should block until the user is finished (the built-in BrowserEditor runs its server synchronously in the calling thread). It isn't expected to return while editing is still in progress.

docs.title: 2. Advertise it as a plugin
docs.text:
nf-meta discovers editor plugins via the nf_meta.editors entry-point group:

[project.entry-points."nf_meta.editors"]
my-editor = "my_editor_package.editor:MyEditor"

Once installed alongside nf-meta, my-editor appears in nf-meta editor --editor without any change to nf-meta itself.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
pip install -e .   # or however your plugin package installs
nf-meta editor --editor my-editor metapipeline.yaml

As with runner plugins, a plugin module that fails to import is skipped with a logged warning rather than a hard failure. Check that first if my-editor doesn't show up as a choice.

docs.title: Cross-workflow references
docs.text:
A param value can reference another workflow's own param via:

${<workflow-id>:<namespace>:<key>}

For example, input: ${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv takes n01's outdir param and substrings it into n02's input param at run time.

  • <workflow-id> must be an id defined under workflows: elsewhere in the same config.
  • <namespace>: only params is currently supported. outputs is reserved syntax for a future capability (referencing a pipeline's declared outputs rather than its input params) and is not yet resolved.
  • <key> is the referenced workflow's own param name.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: nf-meta checks references statically as part of nf-meta validate/on every graph mutation: the referenced workflow must exist, and (where the target pipeline's schema is reachable) the referenced key must be a real parameter on it. A reference to a workflow that doesn't (yet) exist, or that would only exist "after" the referencing workflow in the DAG, is rejected.

docs.title: Resolution at run time
docs.text:
References are only ever resolved inside string-valued params. The token is matched via a regex against the value's text, so a reference can be embedded inside a larger string (${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv) or be the entire value. Numeric/boolean param values can never contain a reference, since they can't contain the literal ${...} text.

The runner resolves each reference just before executing the referencing workflow, preferring an already-resolved (or cached, on --resume) value for the target workflow over its raw config value. See Python runner.

docs.title: YAML representation overview
docs.text:
The nf-meta tooling allows representing a metapipeline, a chain of Nextflow pipeline/module runs, as a single .yaml file. The four top-level keys are:

  • config_version pins the schema this document follows, so the representation can evolve without breaking older configs. See Config reference for the supported range.
  • workflows is a mapping of workflow id to workflow definition. Each entry is one Nextflow pipeline or module run. The flow between workflows is declared per-workflow via from:, not as a separate edge list.
  • globals holds settings applied to every workflow (Nextflow version, profile, shared params, ...).
  • transitions (deprecated) is an older, separate edge-list format, superseded by each workflow's own from: key. It's still readable, but nf-meta logs a deprecation warning and rewrites it to from: the next time the config is saved via the editor.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
config_version: 0.3.0
globals:
  nextflow_version: "25.10"
workflows:
  n01:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: fetchngs-ids.csv
      outdir: out_fetchngs
      nf_core_pipeline: rnaseq
      nf_core_rnaseq_strandedness: auto
  n02:
    from: n01
    name: nf-core/rnaseq
    version: 3.14.0
    params:
      input: ${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv
      genome: GRCh38
      outdir: out_rnaseq

The step n02 runs after n01 (from: n01) and reads its input from n01's own outdir param via the reference ${n01:params:outdir}. See Cross-workflow references for the full syntax. A workflow reference is validated in statically by checking if the connection is possible topologically. An attempt is made to check the workflow references also against each pipeline's own nextflow_schema.json to validate the parameter correctness and types.

docs.title: Validating and running
docs.text:
nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml   # static + schema checks
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml        # executes the chain in dependency order, requires Nextflow

nf-meta validate is the authoritative check: it runs the real Pydantic models plus the tier-2 pipeline-schema checks described above. The config's static shape is also published as a JSON Schema, so your editor can catch structural problems (missing/unknown fields, wrong types) as you type, before you even run validate. It won't catch the params:-level checks though, since those need a network lookup against the pipeline's own schema.

See the quickstart for a minimal end-to-end walkthrough, and Runners for what "executes" actually means (currently: wraps nextflow run/nextflow module run per workflow, in DAG order).

docs.title: Editor autocompletion (JSON Schema)
docs.text:
nf-meta publishes a JSON Schema for the config format. It's what powers inline validation and autocomplete in editors that support the yaml-language-server schema convention. VS Code's YAML extension is the common case.

The schema only covers the config's static shape: Top-level keys, per-workflow fields like name/version/from, required-ness, types. Since this is a structurally flexible declaration format, the schema has no way to know what's valid inside a given workflow's params:. That's checked against the pipeline's own nextflow_schema.json when nf-meta validate is called. This dynamic validation via the cli command gives you information about lines and keys where something is wrong, but you cannot currently use this in your text editor.

Any config saved through the editor has this line added, which enables the static validation in VSCode with the YAML extension (redhat.vscdoe-yaml) by pointing to the JSON-schema: 

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bmds-tue/nf-meta/refs/heads/main/schemas/metapipeline.schema.json
workflows:
  ...

To utilize it in VSCode:

  1. Install the YAML extension (redhat.vscode-yaml).
  2. Add the same # yaml-language-server: $schema=... line as the first line of your .yaml file.
  3. Start typing. Unknown keys, missing required fields, and wrong types are flagged inline, and Ctrl+Space completes valid keys/enum values.

The schema can be re-generated locally with your nf-meta installation.

nf-meta export-schema schemas/metapipeline.schema.json

The $schema=... can also point at a local path relative to the config file instead of the GitHub URL.

docs.title: Config reference
docs.text: Key-by-key reference for the metapipeline .yaml format. See YAML representation overview for how these fit together and Cross-workflow references for the ${...} syntax usable in params values.

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Key Type Required Default Notes config_version string yes — Must be between 0.0.1 and the current maximum (0.3.0). Rejected outside that range. workflows mapping (id → workflow) yes — See Workflow (common fields) below. A list form exists for backward compatibility but is deprecated. globals mapping no none See globals below. transitions list no none Legacy edge list ({source, target} pairs). Deprecated in favor of each workflow's own from:; still readable but triggers a warning.

docs.title: globals
docs.text: Key Type Required Default Notes profile string no none Nextflow -profile applied to every workflow that doesn't set its own profile. Whitespace is stripped. config_file path to an existing .config file no none Passed as a Nextflow -c to every workflow, in addition to any per-workflow config_file. params mapping (str → scalar) no none Merged under each workflow's own params, with the workflow's values taking precedence on key collision. Values must be str/int/float/bool. nextflow_version string, int, or float no none e.g. "25.10", "25.10.4-edge", 25. Checked against the actually-installed nextflow -version before a run; mismatch is reported, not silently ignored.

docs.title: Workflow (common fields)
docs.text:
Every entry under workflows: is one of two types, selected by type: (default nf-pipeline when omitted). These fields apply to both:

Key Type Required Default Notes type nf-pipeline | nf-module no nf-pipeline Selects NfPipeline vs. NfModule below. (id) — yes — Not a field inside the entry; it's the entry's own key under workflows:, e.g. n01:. Referenced by from:, ${id:params:key}, and the CLI's --start/--target. name string, non-empty yes — Pipeline/module name, e.g. nf-core/rnaseq. For nf-core pipelines, also used to auto-resolve url/description. version string, non-empty yes — A release tag (1.12.0, v1.12.0) or a full/short commit SHA (7-40 hex chars). A branch name (e.g. dev, master) is rejected, since reproducibility requires a pinned revision. from string or list of strings no none Id(s) of the workflow(s) that must complete before this one runs. Determines execution (DAG) order. params mapping (str → scalar) no none Passed to the pipeline as -params-file. Values must be str/int/float/bool; real types are preserved through to the generated params file, not stringified. May contain ${...} references (string values only). config_file path to an existing .config file no none Workflow-specific Nextflow -c, in addition to globals.config_file.

docs.title: nf-pipeline additional fields
docs.text:
For a nextflow run-style pipeline step (the default type):

Key Type Required Default Notes url string conditional auto-resolved for nf-core pipelines Required for non-nf-core pipelines (must start with https://). For an nf-core pipeline matched by name, auto-filled from the nf-core pipeline list; an explicit mismatching url is rejected. description string no auto-filled for nf-core pipelines Free text; auto-populated from nf-core's own description when available. params_file path to an existing .yaml/.yml file no none An external base params file. Merged with params at run time (params overrides on key collision) and included in schema validation. profile string no none Overrides globals.profile for this workflow specifically. main_script string no none Alternate entry script within the pipeline repo. Not settable for nf-core pipelines.

docs.title: nf-module additional fields
docs.text:
For a nextflow module run-style step:

Key Type Required Default Notes container_engine docker | singularity | conda | podman no none Passed as -with-<engine>.

docs.title: Legacy transitions: entries
docs.text: Each entry is {source: <id>, target: <id>}, equivalent to adding from: <source> to the target workflow. Prefer from: in new configs; opening and saving a config with legacy transitions: in the editor rewrites it automatically.

docs.title: Runners
docs.text: A runner takes a validated metapipeline graph and actually executes it. nf-meta selects a runner by name (nf-meta run --runner <name>, default python) and dispatches to a registered BaseRunner subclass.

docs.title: Available today
docs.text: • Python runner (python, default): wraps nextflow run/nextflow module run per workflow from this Python process, in DAG order.

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• nf-cascade runner: compile the config into a single daisy-chained Nextflow script, delegating orchestration to nf-cascade. A stub (NfCascadeRunner) exists in the codebase but is not yet implemented.
  • Seqera Platform runner: start and monitor runs by calling a Seqera Platform instance's API with the resolved parameters, rather than shelling out to nextflow locally.
  • Meta-pipeline runner: compile the config into a monolithic Nextflow project that imports the required workflows directly, for the most efficient orchestration and graceful cross-workflow error handling.
  • Notebook runner: transpile the meta-pipeline config into its most interactive form: A Jupyter notebook moving the Workflow runs closer to your downstream analysis.

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text: Runners are pluggable via the same entry-point mechanism as third-party packages: a package registers a BaseRunner subclass under the nf_meta.runners entry-point group, and it becomes selectable via --runner <name> as soon as it's installed, with no changes to nf-meta itself. See Writing a runner.

docs.title: Python runner
docs.text: RUNNER_NAME = "python" (the default). Executes a metapipeline directly from this Python process: for each workflow in dependency (DAG) order, it builds and runs the corresponding nextflow run or nextflow module run command as a subprocess, streaming its output.

docs.title: Caching and --resume
docs.text:
Each workflow's resolved params (after substituting any ${...} references) are cached under --cachedir (default .nf-meta-cache/), keyed by the workflow and a content hash of its definition. nf-meta run --resume:

  • skips a workflow entirely if its working directory already recorded a successful prior run
  • still passes -resume through to Nextflow for workflows that do run, so a partially-completed step doesn't restart from scratch either

This means a failure partway through a long chain doesn't require re-running everything that already succeeded; only the failing step onward, once fixed.

docs.title: Subsetting with --start/--target
docs.text: --start <id> / --target <id> run only the sub-DAG between two workflow ids (inclusive). Cross-boundary references (a workflow inside the subset referencing one excluded from it) are validated before anything runs: if the excluded workflow has no successful cached run to read a resolved value from, the runner refuses to start rather than fail partway through.

docs.title: --stub
docs.text: Passes -stub to Nextflow, replacing each process's script with a no-op stub, which is useful for validating a metapipeline's structure and parameter wiring without real compute. Note: nf-meta places -stub after the pipeline's URL/revision in the generated Nextflow command deliberately, working around a Nextflow CLI argument-order bug (reported upstream) where -stub placed immediately before another option can cause Nextflow to resolve the wrong pipeline.

docs.title: Global params merging
docs.text: globals.params is merged into each workflow's own params before the run (the workflow's own values win on key collision). This happens after caching, so the cache only ever holds workflow-specific resolved values.
